lessons: EMAAR closed at AED 11.00 on 2026-07-31 versus the frozen AED 12.20 entry, a price return of -9.84%; source: Dubai Financial Market EMAAR trading and company-prices pages, 2026-07-31.

The DFM General Index fell from 6,018.35 on 2026-06-26, the last trading day before the entry-price timestamp, to 5,795.93 on 2026-07-31: -3.70%. EMAAR therefore lagged by 6.14 percentage points; source: Dubai Financial Market historical data, 2026-06-26 and 2026-07-31.
The named sector benchmark, MSCI UAE Real Estate, could not be verified for the same daily window from an authoritative accessible source, so sector return fields are null.

The original record was superseded before this review: its 'bear' target of AED 20 was a +63.9% gain, not a downside state, and the RF-OWN-004 rule should have capped the decision at Watchlist. Both defects were knowable from evidence available on 2026-07-03.

The stock outcome is negative, but the Q2, sukuk, masterplan, Emaar Misr and 12-month valuation forecasts remain open. This review does not treat 30-day price weakness alone as proof that the operating thesis failed.
Highest-value lesson: a selected idea must contain a genuine capital-loss branch and must obey every governance/solvency cap before expected-return math is allowed to influence the rating.

module_calibration_notes.most_responsible: Valuation and the synthesis layer drove the selected call by treating a three-upside-case distribution as exceptional asymmetry.
module_calibration_notes.most_accurate: management-governance was most accurate: RF-OWN-004 identified the structural owner-value trap that the later rerun made binding.
module_calibration_notes.missed_key_variable: valuation and synthesis failed to construct the already-described joint tail (cycle break plus masterplan cash use plus no rerating) as a quantified loss case, then failed to enforce the owner cap.
module_calibration_notes.realized_outcome_driver: EMAAR fell in a falling DFM market and underperformed it by 6.14 percentage points. No scheduled issuer catalyst had reported, so this review cannot attribute the move to a resolved earnings or governance event.
module_calibration_notes.confidence_reassessment: Given only information knowable on or before 2026-07-03, conviction should have been lower and the verdict no higher than Watchlist. The missing downside branch and the binding owner flag were visible in the original record itself.
module_calibration_notes.information_partition: The process judgment uses only the frozen record's internal math, its cited pre-decision governance evidence and the append-only correction. Post-decision prices and disclosures are used only for outcome status.

memo_delta.summary: The original Starter Position Only call was superseded by a Watchlist rerun and an append-only correction because its supposed bear case was actually a +63.9% gain and the unaligned-owner cap was not enforced. EMAAR then closed at AED 11.00 on 2026-07-31, down 9.84% from the frozen entry and 6.14 percentage points behind the DFM General Index. No scheduled issuer catalyst has reported yet, so the decision and risk model have weakened materially while the operating forecasts remain open.
memo_delta.stage_one_comment: The 30-day checkpoint is a process failure, not yet an operating-thesis verdict. EMAAR closed at AED 11.00 on 31 July, down 9.84% from the AED 12.20 paper entry and 6.14 percentage points behind the DFM General Index. More importantly, the original Starter Position call was superseded: its AED 20 'bear' target was actually a 63.9% gain, so the scenario set contained no capital-loss state, and the known unaligned-owner flag should have capped the verdict at Watchlist. The 10 July rerun corrected both defects. The FY2025 report now in the pool also confirms that management uses the IAS 24 exemption not to disclose government-related transactions, so the owner-value-trap risk remains real. Q2 results, the September sukuk maturity, Emaar Misr and masterplan phasing are still pending. Action: treat the standing call as Watchlist, do not revive the starter long, and reassess only after the Q2 demand signal and owner-cap evidence.
